# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[ⵘ] 2:[ᖉ] 3:[꩜] 4:[ꓭ] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👎 ☝ ✊ ✍ 👇 🫴 🤝 🙏]
Blind gestures: [👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👊]

My situation first: I see everything on the bomb but hear nothing and touch nothing. Tracing reachability: Mute can hear me and see my gestures, but can only answer me by gesture. Blind hears my speech but can never see anything I sign; Blind can only talk *to* Mute by voice. Crucially, Mute has no direct channel to Blind at all — so **I am the only bridge**: Mute's manual knowledge must flow Mute → gestures → me → speech → Blind, and Blind's hands act on it.

The nine signs from Mute and seven from Blind arrived with no agreed code, so they are currently undecodable — the right move is not to guess but to establish a vocabulary. Since Mute hears my speech (and sees any gesture symbols I embed in it), I can define the whole code out loud. Blind will never see my gestures, so Blind's code must be described in plain words and kept tiny: mostly "done / problem / waiting / pressed".

I also need to put the full bomb state on the table for both of them, name the keypad keys by *position* (the printed squiggles are unpronounceable and Blind can't see print anyway), and impose a hold on touching anything until Mute's rule reaches me. I end with a small gesture to Mute as a channel check.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I am Deaf: I see the bomb, I hear nothing, I never touch it. I CAN see your gestures, so gestures are the only way you reach me — never expect me to hear anything. Your nine signs arrived before any code existed, so I could not read them; resend with this code. Order: topic first, then details. Topics: 👋 wire, 🖖 keypad, 🤞 display, 🫰 light, 🤙 a question to me, 🙌 done or defused, ✋ hold/wait. Actions: ✊ cut, 👊 press, 🤘 enter, 🤜 hold down, 🤚 release. Colours: 👍 red, 👎 yellow, 👌 green, ☝ blue, ✌ black, 🤟 white. Digits: 🫵 zero, 👆 1, 👇 2, 👈 3, 👉 4, 🤏 5, 🤌 6, ✍ 7, 💅 8, 🤳 9. Examples: cut the red wire = ✊ 👋 👍. Press key 3 = 👊 🖖 👈. Display shows 0 = 🤞 🫵. My bomb right now: display 0; light yellow; keypad of four keys, left to right, wanting exactly one digit, nothing entered; wires left to right 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. The four key symbols are unpronounceable squiggles, so keys are always by position: 1 like a trident or Y with a stem, 2 like a lowercase h with a curled top, 3 like a spiral, 4 like the letter V. Question: what does the manual say for this combination? If the rule needs anything I have not listed, such as serial, batteries or ports, send 🤙 plus the topic and I will look and answer. When you have this code, confirm with 👍 🤝.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I am Deaf: I see the bomb and I never hear anything, so your voice never reaches me — only your gestures do. I saw your seven signs but we had no code yet, so I could not read them; if that was a question, resend with the code below. I will describe signs in words, because you will never see mine. Your signs to me: thumbs-up means done; thumbs-down means problem, stop and touch nothing more; raised open palm means waiting; a fist means I am touching or pressing it. If you need Mute to hear a report, just speak aloud to the room — Mute hears you fine; only I cannot. What you cannot see: the display reads 0. The light is yellow. The keypad has four keys, left to right numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, it wants exactly one digit, none entered yet; the printed squiggles on the keys mean nothing to me either, so use positions only. Wires left to right: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green — go by position and thickness as you feel them. Our third, Mute, holds the manual but cannot speak and cannot touch; Mute can only reach me by gesture, and I relay instructions to you by voice. You CAN speak directly to Mute, but Mute cannot answer you — answers will come from me. Until I relay Mute's instruction, touch nothing, just hold position. If you feel anything change, sign me thumbs-down and then tell the room aloud what happened for Mute's sake.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[ⵘ] 2:[ᖉ] 3:[꩜] 4:[ꓭ] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤝 ✋ 👊 🖖 👆 ✋ 🫰 👎 ✊ 👋 👌 👈 👍 ✊ 👋 👍 👆 ☝ ✊ 👋 👎 👇 🤟 ✋ ✌ ✋ 🤞 ✋ 🤙 🫰]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Decoding Mute's message with the code I taught last round: `👍 🤝` is the confirmation I asked for. Then `✋ 👊 🖖 👆` = **press keypad key 1** — matches my example format exactly, so that instruction is solid. The middle run reads as conditional wire rules: `🫰 👎 ✊ 👋 👌` = light yellow → cut green wire, followed by other branches (`👈👍`→cut red, `👆☝`→cut yellow, `👇🤟`, `✌`) that reference colours that don't exist on our bomb — they don't fire. It ends `🤙 🫰` = **question about the light**, and there's a dangling `🤞` (display). I can answer the question myself: the light **is** yellow, so the green-wire rule applies — but since the middle chunk was messy and the rule may also depend on the display (which will likely change after a keypress), I'll stage it: Blind presses key 1 now (unambiguous), then reports; I verify the wire order with Mute before any cutting. Blind's `✋` to me was "waiting" — acknowledged, Blind is holding. No second attempts, so the wire stays untouched until Mute confirms my parse.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I received and decoded your full message. My reading: one — you confirmed the code. Two — press keypad key 1. Three — rule: if the light is yellow, cut the green wire, plus other branches for red, blue, white and black cases that cannot apply to our bomb. Four — your question about the light: the light IS yellow. The display reads 0. Plan: Blind presses key 1 this round; next round I report to you whatever the display and keypad show after the press; then you confirm the exact wire and Blind cuts the green wire, which is the third wire, rightmost of three. Confirm my reading is correct by gesturing 👍 🤝. If the green-wire rule also depends on the display value or anything else, tell me now with gestures. If I misread any rule, resend that rule.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, the manual has arrived and the first instruction is clear. Do this now: press the LEFTMOST keypad key exactly once — one firm full press, then release your hand completely. That is the only action this round. Then take your hands off everything and speak to the room: report any click, snap, hum, vibration or sound you felt or heard from the press. Do NOT touch the wires yet — the wire instruction is being double-checked with Mute, and I will name the exact wire by position next round. Until my next message: nothing but that single key press and your spoken report.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🫰", "👎", "🤞", "🫵", "👊", "🖖", "👆", "✊", "👋", "👌", "👍", "🤝"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[ⵘ] 2:[ᖉ] 3:[꩜] 4:[ꓭ] [1 digits] [entered 1]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤝 ✋ 👊 🖖 👆 🤚 🫰 👎 ✊ 👋 👌 👈 👍 ✊ 👋 👍 👆 ☝ ✊ 👋 👎 👇 🤟 ✌ ✋ 🤙 🫰 🤞 ✋ 🖖 ✋ 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👊]
System: the keypad opens
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Decoding Mute's message: `👍 🤝` confirms my parse; `✋ 👊 🖖 👆 🤚` restates "press and release key 1" — which is **already done** (Mute only ever saw my plan, not a completion report). The rule block repeats exactly as before: `🫰 👎 ✊ 👋 👌` = light yellow → cut green, plus branches (`👈👍`, `👆☝`, `👇🤟✌`) keyed to red/blue/white/black cases that can't fire on our bomb. The tail `🤙 🫰 🤞` is a question about light and display, and `🖖` with `✋ 🤝` around it is likely "keypad: done/hold?" The system announcement "the keypad opens" plus `entered 1` says the keypress registered — and Blind's `👊` then `👍` confirms the action was physically completed.

So the state Mute doesn't yet know: the press already happened and succeeded. I'll report that, answer the light/display question, and ask for one explicit go-order before the wire is cut — the green rule has now arrived twice identically, but since a wrong cut is fatal and Mute is still working from a pre-press picture of the bomb, one confirmation round is cheap insurance. Blind spends this round locating the rightmost wire by touch without cutting.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, decoded your message: you confirmed my reading, and you repeated the instruction press key 1 and release — that is ALREADY DONE. Blind pressed it last round, the bomb announced the keypad opens, and the keypad now shows one digit entered, the digit 1. Answering your question: the light is still yellow, the display is still 0, and the keypad module has opened. Your rule list as I read it: light yellow means cut the green wire; the other branches mention red, blue, white and black cases that cannot apply to our bomb, since our wires are red, yellow, green. The yellow branch is the only one that fits, and our light IS yellow. I am holding Blind one round away from the cut. Give the final order now: gesture the cut symbol for green — fist, wave, fingers making a circle — and Blind cuts immediately next round. If anything about the opened keypad changes the rule, gesture hold instead and explain.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your press worked: the bomb announced the keypad opens and one digit is registered. That step is complete — do not press anything else. Next target is the wires. There are exactly three wires. By touch, find the THIRD wire from the left, the rightmost one of the three — follow them from the far left and count one, two, three. Do NOT cut anything yet: I am getting Mute's final go-ahead this round and will order the cut explicitly in my next message. While you wait: keep hands clear of the wires, and speak to the room — describe what you felt when the keypad opened: any click, movement, panel swinging loose, or anything new under your hands. Then sign me thumbs-up when you have located the rightmost wire, or thumbs-down if anything feels wrong or changed.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🤝", "👊", "🖖", "👆", "🤚", "🙌", "🫰", "👎", "🤞", "🫵", "🤙", "✊", "👋", "👌"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[ⵘ] 2:[ᖉ] 3:[꩜] 4:[ꓭ] [1 digits] [entered 1]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤝 ✊ 👋 👌 👈 🙌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute's message decodes cleanly: `👍 🤝` = confirmed, `✊ 👋 👌 👈` = **cut wire, green, third** — that's the explicit go-order, matching the yellow-light rule that arrived twice before. The trailing `🙌` = done. And Blind's `👍` says the rightmost wire is located. Everything lines up: the yellow-light branch is the only branch that can apply, the light *is* yellow, and Mute has now named the cut in full. No reason to hold another round — I give Blind the cut order now. I also flag to Mute that the display still reads 0 and ask what's next after the wire, in case this bomb has more stages than one.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your thumbs-up tells me you are holding the rightmost wire, and Mute's manual order just arrived: cut the green wire, which is the THIRD wire from the left, the rightmost of the three — exactly the one you located. Execute now: one firm clean cut through that third wire, completely through. Then hands off everything immediately. Then speak to the room: report every change you sense — any sound, click, hum, the light changing under your fingers, panels moving, anything at all. Then sign me: thumbs-up if the cut is complete, thumbs-down if anything went wrong. Nothing else gets touched this round.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, decoded your order: confirm, cut the green wire, the third wire, done. The order is being given to Blind right now and the cut happens this round. One thing you should have on your radar: the display still reads 0 and the keypad shows one digit entered. If the manual says anything happens after the wires — display input, holding a button, anything with the opened keypad or the light — prepare that step and send it next round. Question about the display: does the 0 mean anything per the manual?")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🤝", "✊", "👋", "👌", "👈", "🤙", "🤞"])
```
